claim: Organize a working reference board by functional purpose such as form and color, and annotate those groups so a source can be retrieved for the decision it supports.
supporting_evidence: OBSERVED: the PureRef montage visibly groups bird, fish, and insect images and adds text notes including Main Form and Main Colour. INSTRUCTOR CLAIM: the course covers importing, manipulating, organizing, and using references beside another application. INTERPRETATION: role labels are more actionable than an unsorted image pile. HYPOTHESIS: property-scoped labels will reduce use of weak references for unrelated claims.
rejected_alternative: Treat every gathered image as equally active and authoritative

claim: Use scene-aligned Blender references for calibrated orthographic construction and an external board for broad comparison, notes, and auxiliary references; the two layers solve different problems.
supporting_evidence: OBSERVED: importing in perspective produces a diagonally aligned card; importing in Front Orthographic aligns it to an axis. Later, PureRef is kept as a separate always-on-top board with crop and flip controls. INSTRUCTOR CLAIM: orthographic import fixes the Blender setup while PureRef manages many references. INTERPRETATION: these are complementary reference layers. HYPOTHESIS: separating them reduces scene clutter without losing broad evidence.
rejected_alternative: Force all collected references into Blender or keep all alignment-critical references only outside Blender
reason: Broad evidence management and axis-calibrated construction have different interaction and persistence needs.

claim: Assign every secondary reference a named property role instead of allowing it to influence the whole target implicitly.
supporting_evidence: OBSERVED: the artist selects separate ArtStation works specifically for facial stylization, hair flow, and color saturation. INSTRUCTOR CLAIM: each secondary source should be chosen for a target-specific feature. INTERPRETATION: source-to-property mapping prevents accidental authority expansion. HYPOTHESIS: explicit claims will make reference conflicts and missing evidence easier to detect.
rejected_alternative: Let an attractive source silently control form, construction, detail, and material together

claim: For exact reconstruction, same-target factual references control geometry; multi-source creative synthesis is reserved for declared design or adaptation tasks and cannot override target dimensions or construction.
supporting_evidence: OBSERVED: the artist combines a real portrait anchor with separate stylized face, hair, and palette sources to create a new portrait. INSTRUCTOR CLAIM: multiple sources produce original synthesis. INTERPRETATION: this is useful for ideation but conflicts with fidelity to one manufactured object. HYPOTHESIS: declaring task intent before sourcing will prevent variant mixing in reconstruction.
rejected_alternative: Apply creative multi-source synthesis indiscriminately to a specific real-world target
reason: A method for originality is not automatically a method for factual reconstruction.

claim: A structured reference record should keep the visual evidence link or timestamp adjacent to the property claim it supports, enabling immediate audit rather than detached notes.
supporting_evidence: OBSERVED: a mechanics spreadsheet stores stable fields and linked YouTube clips, then a local visual wiki presents the same data with playable GIFs. INSTRUCTOR CLAIM: direct clips make visual verification immediate. INTERPRETATION: claims and media should remain joined through provenance. HYPOTHESIS: this will reduce unsupported geometric inferences in reference modeling.
rejected_alternative: Store conclusions separately from the source evidence needed to audit them

claim: Choose reference fidelity according to task intent: faithful study, controlled adaptation, and composite ideation require different evidence and acceptance rules.
supporting_evidence: OBSERVED: six animation examples range from close live-action matching to timing edits and composite mood boards. INSTRUCTOR CLAIM: there is no universal reference style; it should fit project needs. INTERPRETATION: static modeling likewise needs an explicit reconstruction/adaptation/design intent. HYPOTHESIS: intent-specific gates will outperform one universal reference score.
rejected_alternative: Use one fidelity policy for every reference-driven task

claim: A source can provide one abstract property such as value, color relationship, or mechanical detail without becoming authoritative for its literal subject geometry.
supporting_evidence: OBSERVED: a snowy sunset is used for color/value relationships while NASA launch-pad photos are separately cropped for mechanical detail. INSTRUCTOR CLAIM: a source need not match the literal subject when only its palette or natural light relationships are needed. INTERPRETATION: authority is property-specific. HYPOTHESIS: purpose-scoped claims prevent material/style sources from authorizing dimensions.
rejected_alternative: Treat every property visible in a source as equally transferable to the target
